transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. — nice to meet you. What brings you in today?
Nice to meet you, Doctor. For the last couple of years I just can’t think clearly or make up my mind about anything, even simple stuff. It just feels like my brain is always stuck in slow gear.
Have you also been feeling depressed or losing interest/pleasure in things most days, or is it mainly the thinking and concentration problem?

It's definitely more than just the thinking issues—most days I feel this heavy, gray cloud hanging over me, leaving me feeling empty even when good things happen. I've also lost all my energy and interest in things I used to love, like playing guitar or shooting hoops, because I just feel so wiped out all the time.
How much has this been affecting your daily life—are you still able to work, study, and take care of yourself, or have you been unable to do these because of how you feel?

It's really affecting everything. I'm turning in my night-class assignments late and my grades are slipping, and at the clinic I'm moving so slowly that I need coworkers to double-check my work. I've also completely stopped volunteering or making plans with my friends because I just feel too drained.
Have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, thoughts of hurting yourself, or any plans to end your life?
No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or ending my life. Even though I feel really hopeless and stuck about my future, I've never thought about doing anything like that.
Do your symptoms make it impossible to do most day-to-day activities, like work, school, or self-care, or are you still able to function but with a lot of difficulty?

I'm still able to function, but it requires immense effort and I am struggling significantly. I'm barely keeping up with my night classes and turning assignments in late, and at the clinic, I move so slowly that my coworkers have to double-check my work. It basically takes everything I have just to do the bare minimum, so I've stopped making plans with friends.
Have these symptoms become so severe that you are unable to do most of your usual work, school, or self-care tasks, or are you still able to do them with great difficulty?

I'm still trying to do them, but it's with great difficulty and I'm falling behind on everything. At the clinic, I move so slowly that coworkers have to double-check my work, and my night-class grades are slipping because I'm turning assignments in late. I've also stopped volunteering or making plans with friends because I'm just too drained.
Are you still able to do most of your usual work, school, and self-care tasks, even if it is very hard, or have you become unable to do most of them?

I am still technically doing them, but my performance has suffered a lot. I still go to work and try to study, but I'm turning assignments in late, needing coworkers to double-check my tasks, and I've stopped seeing friends because I'm just too drained.
Would you say your depression has made it impossible to do most of your usual work, school, or self-care tasks, or are you still able to do them but with great difficulty?

It's not impossible, but I am doing them with extreme difficulty. I'm still barely managing to get by, but my grades are slipping from late assignments and my coworkers have to double-check my slow work at the clinic. I've also had to stop volunteering or seeing my friends because I'm just too drained.
Would you say your symptoms have made it impossible for you to do most of your usual work, school, or self-care tasks, or are you still able to do them but with great difficulty?

I can still do them, but it requires a massive effort and I am struggling significantly. I'm turning in my night-class assignments late, my grades are slipping, and my coworkers at the clinic have to double-check my work because I'm moving so slowly. I've also had to pull back from volunteering and making plans with my friends.
Would you say your symptoms make it impossible to do most of your usual work, school, or self-care tasks, or are you still able to do them but with great difficulty?

I'm still able to do them, but it's with great difficulty. I'm barely getting through my shifts at the clinic and my night classes, but I move so slowly that coworkers have to double-check me and my grades are slipping. I've also stopped volunteering and seeing my friends because I just don't have the energy.
Would you say your symptoms make it impossible for you to do most of your work, school, or self-care tasks, or are you still able to do them but with great difficulty?

I'm still able to do them, but only with great difficulty because getting through the day feels like dragging myself through mud. My grades are slipping from turning in night-class assignments late, and at the clinic I move so slowly that my coworkers have to double-check my simple tasks.
Do your symptoms make it impossible for you to do most of your usual work, school, or self-care tasks, or are you still able to do them but with great difficulty?

I am still able to do them, but it takes a lot of effort and I do them with great difficulty. My grades are dropping because I turn night-class assignments in late, and my coworkers have to double-check my slow work at the clinic. I've also stopped volunteering and making plans with friends because I'm just too exhausted.
Do your symptoms make it impossible for you to do most of your usual work, school, or self-care tasks, or are you still able to do them but with great difficulty?

I can still manage to do them, but it is with great difficulty. At the clinic, I move so slowly that my coworkers have to double-check my simple tasks, and my night-class grades are slipping because I turn assignments in late. I've also stopped volunteering and making plans with friends because I'm just too drained.
Do your symptoms make it impossible for you to do most of your usual work, school, or self-care tasks, or are you still able to do them but with great difficulty?

I am still able to do them, but it is incredibly difficult and I'm barely getting by. I drag myself through my shifts and night classes, but I move so slowly at the clinic that coworkers have to double-check my work, and I'm constantly turning in assignments late.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m Dr. — nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a multi-year depressive syndrome with persistent low mood/emptiness, marked loss of interest and pleasure, low energy/fatigue, psychomotor slowing, and impaired concentration/decision-making, causing clear academic, occupational, and social impairment. He remains able to function, but only with great difficulty, which is most consistent with a moderate depressive episode (ICD-10 F32.1). No suicidal ideation or psychotic symptoms were endorsed.
